_readme: Business facts live here and nowhere else. The page, the hours table, the open/closed badge and the Google structured data all read this file, so changing a number here changes it everywhere at once.
name: Jill's Diner

address.landmark: Between Rural King and Disc Replay, in the old RadioShack spot.

story.title: A Columbus diner since 1952
story.lede: Since 1952 the names over the door have changed. The diner hasn't: eggs on the flattop, coffee in the pot, and regulars who know each other by name.

timeline.title: It starts on Seventh Street
timeline.text: Gerald I. Davis, a Marine and World War II veteran, opens his grill at 421 Seventh Street, downtown.

timeline.title: Bennie and Carolyn
timeline.text: After twenty years Davis sells to Bennie and Carolyn Stott, and the counter keeps going.

timeline.title: Sadie's, then Kramer's
timeline.text: Sadie Cress takes over, followed by Joe and Debbie Kramer. New names over the door, same little diner.

timeline.title: It becomes Jill's
timeline.text: Jill buys the diner in February 2008. It has been a family place ever since.

timeline.title: A new home on National Road
timeline.text: After 73 years downtown, the diner packs up and reopens at 3005 N. National Road. Same diner, new address.

regulars: Everybody eats here: first responders, construction crews, plumbers, retirees, Bible study groups, and families with little ones in tow.
